seo.title: Multiply Labs | A clearer story for robotic biomanufacturing
seo.description: A tailored product story preview for Multiply Labs’ robotic biomanufacturing platform, designed to set up a focused conversation about instruments, process fit and scale.

hero.title: Your process.
hero.body: Four robotic arms. Twelve modular instrument towers. A system designed around the GMP instruments teams already use. This focused story makes the platform easier to understand before a conversation about process fit and scale.
hero.imageAlt: Multiply Labs product image showing four robotic arms operating inside a modular robotic cluster; image from the company product page.

concept.eyebrow: A complex platform, made easier to follow.
concept.title: Give each stakeholder the same clear starting point.
concept.body: Show the system at a glance, then let Multiply Labs’ team take the conversation into the prospect’s instruments, therapy and scale goals.

research.body: Four robotic arms and twelve modular instrument towers in a cluster under 600 sq ft, according to Multiply Labs.

journey.eyebrow: Three parts of the platform story
journey.title: Start with the instruments.
journey.body: Connect what a buyer already knows—their equipment and process—to the role of robotics and the information captured for review.
journey.navigationLabel: Follow the cluster from instruments to process records

steps.title: Start with familiar equipment.
steps.copy: Multiply Labs lists integrations and examples including Rotea, Dynacellect and Heracell VIOS. Use one relevant example to show how robotic touchpoints can fit around the instruments a prospect already uses.
steps.imageAlt: Multiply Labs product image of its four-arm robotic cluster; public product imagery, illustrative in this story.

steps.title: Show the system’s role.
steps.copy: Four robotic arms coordinate tasks such as liquid handling, dispensing and transfers inside the cluster. Keep the animation at platform level; confirm any customer-specific sequence with the technical team.
steps.imageAlt: Multiply Labs product image showing a robotic arm holding a syringe inside its cluster.

steps.title: Close with the information trail.
steps.copy: The Process Creator App helps scientists build and modify processes. Multiply Labs says its software captures process data and sends electronic records into quality workflows.
steps.imageAlt: Multiply Labs product image of an operator using an interface at the robotic cluster.

response.title: Answer the big question before the technical deep dive.
response.body: Use one clear visual to orient commercial, process and quality stakeholders. Then tailor the walkthrough to a prospect’s equipment, manufacturing protocol and requirements.
response.beforeMessage: How would this work with the process we already run?
response.beforeNote: Start with their instruments, process and scale goals.

tabs.label: Existing equipment
tabs.question: Will the cluster work with our GMP instruments?
tabs.answer: Multiply Labs says its cluster is designed around instruments teams already use. A tailored technical walkthrough can assess a prospect’s specific equipment and touchpoints.

tabs.label: Process execution
tabs.question: What parts of our process can be automated?
tabs.answer: The platform is built to orchestrate robotic work around manufacturing instruments. The product team can map relevant unit operations to a prospect’s actual process.

tabs.label: Records and quality
tabs.question: How are process records captured?
tabs.answer: Multiply Labs describes software that collects process data and delivers electronic records into quality workflows. The quality team can discuss the details and fit.

comparison.title: Make the platform easier to picture.
comparison.body: The story format: establish the system-level context first, then use the live discussion to explore a specific manufacturing process.

process.title: A review path built around your platform

faqs.question: Is the generated video a recording of Multiply Labs’ robot?
faqs.answer: No. The motion is AI-generated and illustrative. The page uses public product photography separately as product reference; the video does not show the actual equipment or a verified manufacturing sequence.

faqs.question: Are the product facts from Multiply Labs?
faqs.answer: Yes. The details on this page are based on Multiply Labs’ public product and funding pages. Any customer-specific workflow, performance figure or regulatory wording should be confirmed by the company before external publication.

faqs.question: Why make a short story before a walkthrough?
faqs.answer: It can give commercial, process and quality stakeholders the same starting picture, so the walkthrough can focus on their instruments, process and scale questions.

faqs.question: What is the current preview based on?
faqs.answer: Publicly available Multiply Labs product information and imagery, plus generated illustrative motion and an English voice-over. It has not been commissioned or approved by Multiply Labs.

faqs.question: What would a final customer-approved version need?
faqs.answer: A confirmed audience and use case, approved visual references, technical review of the script, and final sign-off from the relevant product, engineering and quality stakeholders.

footer.disclosure: Independent product story preview based on Multiply Labs’ public materials. Generated motion is illustrative and is not a product demo or verified process.

trigger.title: A platform story for the next stage of scale.
trigger.body: Multiply Labs announced $75 million in Series B funding to expand manufacturing capacity and advance its product roadmap as it moves from clinical-stage deployments toward commercial-scale production. This preview focuses on the system story behind that next stage.
